secretName.description: The NAME of a secret, delivered as `secrets.source` says: `valkey/password`, `issuer/state-secret`. A value is never in the document.

url.description: An http or https URL with a host and no credentials: a password in a URL is a secret in the file, and a secret is named, never carried.

description: The configuration of `sluis serve`, the one process of sluis: the issuer, the console and the directory hub and, under `controllers`, the GitHub and Slack controllers. On Kubernetes it is one Deployment; on AWS Lambda it is one function. Secrets are never in this file: a field ending in ...Secret holds the NAME of a secret, which `secrets` says how to deliver, and a field ending in ...File holds a path (a credential the platform mounts and rotates). Telemetry is the OTEL_* environment, not configuration.

adapters.description: Names the adapter of single concerns, over the preset and the `ports` keys. The names and what each needs are in the matrix of docs/reference/adapters.md.

audit.description: The adapter for the audit sink, replacing the preset's.

adapter.description: The adapter's name, as the compatibility matrix lists it.

settings.description: The adapter's own settings (an object; the adapter refuses a key it does not know).

blobs.description: The adapter for blobs, replacing the preset's.

trigger.description: The adapter for the "run a pass now" trigger, replacing the preset's.

allowInsecure.description: Accept a plain-http issuer URL, for a local run.

apiVersion.description: Which version of which document this is. sluis.truvity.github.io/sluis/v3 is the one service document: the process that serves the issuer and the console and, under `controllers`, runs the GitHub and Slack controllers. A binary still reads the v2 `serve` document (and v1, which has no apiVersion) as this document with no controllers (docs/reference/configuration.md).

audit.description: The audit installation this service records to. Unset keeps the trail in the log only.

audience.description: The client whose audience the Audit page's tokens carry.

forwardedForTrustedHops.description: How many of the deployment's own proxies append to X-Forwarded-For; zero records the peer.

queryURL.description: The query service, for the console's Audit page. Its own setting: it needs no `writer`, so the page works with the `sqs` and `log` sinks. A path prefix (`https://audit.example/sluis`) is kept and the procedure path appended.

tokenFile.description: This workload's projected service-account token, presented on every call.

cluster.description: Names this cluster in a ServiceAccount's subject. A pod cannot discover it; unset keeps the older unqualified subject.

console.description: Where the console is published, for the sign-in that starts there.

awsAudience.description: The audience an AWS role's web identity token must be minted for to be a bearer at the console (a Lambda controller). Its own, distinct from the AWS federation file's, so a token for token exchange is no proof here and the reverse. Default `<issuerURL>/console`.

client.description: The client id the console signs in as.

origin.description: The console's origin, when it is not the issuer's.

controllers.description: The controllers this process runs beside the issuer and the console, each in its own loop. A controller that is absent is off. Which organisations and workspaces a running controller may CHANGE is the policy document's `controllers.<kind>.enabledOrgs` and `enabledWorkspaces`, as before. A controller reads the console's API as a workload, so the policy's exchange must admit its proof (a ServiceAccount token on Kubernetes, the function role's web identity token on Lambda).

github.description: The GitHub controller: makes each GitHub organisation's teams match the policy's github table.

appsDir.description: One file per connected organisation: its App's credentials. Read only with `ports.adapter: legacy`; with another adapter they are on the State port.

console.description: How the controller proves itself to the console, when the pod's `tokenFile` is not the way.

aws.description: The function role's AWS outbound web identity token (`sts:GetWebIdentityToken`), re-minted every four minutes. The console's issuer must federate the account, and its policy must declare an `aws` matcher for the role.

audience.description: The audience requested from STS. It must equal `console.awsAudience` (default `<issuerURL>/console`), NOT the audience of the issuer's AWS federation file.

consoleURL.description: The console's API, which answers who holds a group. Unset is `publicURL`. On Kubernetes it is this release's own Service, which the chart writes.

recordsDir.description: The console's records, mounted. Read only with `ports.adapter: legacy`.

tokenFile.description: This pod's projected ServiceAccount token, presented to the console and read afresh on every call.

slack.description: The Slack controller: makes each Slack workspace's user groups match the policy's slack table.

console.description: How the controller proves itself to the console, when the pod's `tokenFile` is not the way.

aws.description: The function role's AWS outbound web identity token (`sts:GetWebIdentityToken`), re-minted every four minutes. The console's issuer must federate the account, and its policy must declare an `aws` matcher for the role.

audience.description: The audience requested from STS. It must equal `console.awsAudience` (default `<issuerURL>/console`), NOT the audience of the issuer's AWS federation file.

consoleURL.description: The console's API, which answers who holds a group. Unset is `publicURL`. On Kubernetes it is this release's own Service, which the chart writes.

credentialsDir.description: One file per connected workspace: the app's credentials and its bot token. Read only with `ports.adapter: legacy`; with another adapter they are on the State port.

recordsDir.description: The console's records, mounted. Read only with `ports.adapter: legacy`.

tokenFile.description: This pod's projected ServiceAccount token, presented to the console and read afresh on every call.

demo.description: Two tenants held in memory, which need no credential and no network.

directory.description: The corporate directories this deployment declares: each adopted at start (the console connects the others). Unset declares none.

workspaces.description: The declared workspaces. One that cannot be adopted stops the service.

items.description: A workspace: deliberately thin. Its domains and the tenant's own id are discovered.

id.description: The backend's tenant id. Optional: given, the adoption checks it.

keySecret.description: The secret the service-account key is: `directory/<id>/key`.

serve.description: Narrows the tenant to these domains. Empty serves every domain discovered.

syncGroups.description: Narrows the tenant to these groups. Empty keeps every group in the served domains.

exchange.description: How the token exchange verifies workloads. Whom it trusts (the clusters, the AWS accounts, the GitHub owners) is the policy document's `exchange`.

audience.description: The audience a workload token must be minted for. Defaults to `release`, so two issuers in one cluster cannot accept each other's proofs.

freshness.description: How the directory's snapshot is kept current.

freshnessWindow.description: How old a snapshot may be and still be answered from.

probeInterval.description: How often the directory is probed.

refreshInterval.description: How often a snapshot is refreshed.

groupsScoping.description: How far this installation has moved toward per-audience `groups` scoping: `off`, `report` or `enforce`.

inCluster.description: Prove recovery against the cluster the pod runs in. Set by a deployment that turns recovery on.

instance.description: The installation's name, bound into the default encryption context of `keys` ({instance, purpose}): stable and not secret, because a ciphertext made under it opens only with it. Unset is `release`.

issuerURL.description: The issuer: baked into every token and every relying party's trust, so there is no default. No trailing slash is kept.

keys.description: Which key serves which purpose. Keys are named by alias (KMS) or by name (transit), never by ARN or key id. See the package documentation of github.com/truvity/sluis/storage/keys.

oneOf.description: An alias such as alias/audit-seal (kms) or a transit key name. An ARN or a key id is refused.

context.description: The encryption context: "default" sends {instance, purpose}; "off" sends none; an object is sent as is.

key.description: An alias such as alias/audit-seal (kms) or a transit key name. An ARN or a key id is refused.

keys.title: keys

lifetimes.description: How long what the issuer hands out lives.

absolute.description: A session, at most. Positive, and at least `token`: a session has to end SOMETIME after sign-in, and an access token cannot outlive the session that grants it.

agent.description: The refresh chains of clients the policy marks `session: agent`, such as MCP hosts (docs/decisions/0040). Their chains are held to these instead of `refresh` and `absolute`.

absolute.description: An agent chain, at most, from `auth_time`. Positive, and at most 2160h (90 days).

access.description: The longest an agent client's access or ID token lives. Positive, and at most 1h.

refresh.description: An agent chain's idle limit. Positive, and at most `absolute`.

hold.description: How long a removal is held before it takes effect.

session.description: The console's own session cookie, capped at `absolute`.

login.description: How a person signs in to the console.

directory.description: Sign in with the corporate directory.

forwarded.description: A sign-in an authenticating proxy has already done.

emailHeader.description: The header that carries the signed-in address.

oauthClient.description: The OAuth client registered once with the directory backend: it drives both admin consent and operator sign-in.

id.description: The client id, for a local run. Not a secret.

idKey.description: The key of the id in that Secret.

provider.description: Names the client's secrets: providers/google/<provider>/client-secret, and providers/google/<provider>/client-id unless `id` gives it. One segment of a secret's name.

secretKey.description: The key of the secret in that Secret.

secretName.description: The Kubernetes Secret the client is declared in, which the console shows and cannot change.

platform.description: What this installation has to build on. The answers pick a preset (the decision tree in docs/explanation/ports.md), and start refuses an adapter that needs an answer that is no. Absent, the `ports` keys decide and nothing is checked against the platform.

aws.description: AWS is available: its credentials, DynamoDB, S3, SSM, KMS, SQS and EventBridge.

replicas.description: How many replicas share this installation's state. Above 1 start refuses an adapter that keeps its data in the process (`memory`).

runtime.description: Where sluis itself runs. Absent: `kubernetes` with a cluster, else `lambda` on AWS, else `process`.

policy.description: The policy document this service decides by. Unset is the built-in two groups, or the demonstration policy under `demo`.

file.description: The policy document: the one canonical file `sluisctl policy render` writes (schemas/config/policy.schema.json). Read once, at start: a change is a new instance.

ports.description: The adapters behind the storage ports (docs/explanation/ports.md).

adapter.description: `legacy` keeps state where it has always been kept: the namespace's ConfigMaps and Secrets and, when `valkey` is set, Valkey. `memory` keeps all of it in this process, which a restart loses: for a local run and the demonstration, and not with `store: kubernetes` or `valkey`.  `dynamodb` keeps the same in one DynamoDB table (`ports.dynamodb`), with the platform's credentials, and takes its Blob from `legacy` unless `ports.blob` names its own.

blob.description: Replaces the Blob port (status reports, directory snapshots) with an adapter of its own, whatever `ports.adapter` is. Absent, the Blob is `ports.adapter`'s.

adapter.description: `s3` keeps the blobs in an S3 bucket.

s3.description: Where the S3 adapter keeps its objects. Credentials are the platform's (EKS Pod Identity, IRSA, a Lambda role) and are never configured here.

bucket.description: The bucket. It must exist, with public access blocked.

endpoint.description: Overrides the S3 address: LocalStack or an S3-compatible store.

kmsKey.description: A KMS key id, ARN or alias for server-side encryption (SSE-KMS) of every write. Absent, the bucket's default encryption applies.

pathStyle.description: Addresses the bucket in the path and not the host name, which LocalStack and most S3-compatible stores need.

prefix.description: A key prefix inside the bucket, for an installation that shares it. Names are `<prefix>/reports/<target>` and `<prefix>/snapshots/<directory>`.

region.description: The bucket's region. Absent, the SDK's own resolution (`AWS_REGION`).

dynamodb.description: The DynamoDB table of the `dynamodb` adapter: one table with a string partition key `pk`, a string sort key `sk` and the TTL attribute `expires`. Credentials are the platform's (EKS Pod Identity, IRSA, a Lambda role) and are never configured here.

create.description: Create the table (on-demand, TTL on `expires`) at start when it is not there, for a test or a development installation. Off, the table must exist: production uses the one the infrastructure code made, and the role needs `dynamodb:DescribeTable` on it.

endpoint.description: Overrides the DynamoDB address: LocalStack or DynamoDB Local.

region.description: The table's region. Absent, the SDK's own resolution (`AWS_REGION`).

export.description: The store the copies of `exports` are written to (docs/decisions/0034). Absent, nothing is copied out of the service, and `exports` must be empty.

adapter.description: `openbao` writes to a KV version 2 mount of an OpenBao. `memory` keeps the copies in this process and is for a test or the demonstration.

openbao.description: The OpenBao the copies are written to. Nothing is contacted at start: an OpenBao that is down must not stop the service, since a copy is never a dependency.

address.description: The server, https only and with no path: `https://openbao.example`. A token and a login JWT cross this connection.

auth.description: How the service logs in, inside each namespace it writes to. The `kubernetes` and `jwt` methods take the same request (`auth/<mount>/login` with a role and a JWT) and differ in the mount they default to and where the JWT comes from.

method.description: `kubernetes`: the Kubernetes auth method, with this pod's ServiceAccount token. `jwt`: the JWT/OIDC method, with a token the platform projects (a ServiceAccount token of another audience, or, on AWS Lambda, the web identity token of outbound federation) from `tokenFile`.

mount.description: The auth method's mount path in each namespace. Absent, the method's name.

role.description: The role the login asks for. It must be bound to this workload's identity and carry a policy that reads, creates, updates and patches only the paths `exports` names.

tokenFile.description: Where the JWT is read from, afresh on every login. Absent with `kubernetes`, the pod's ServiceAccount token; required with `jwt`.

caFile.description: A PEM bundle of the authorities that sign the server's certificate, in place of the system's.

namespace.description: The OpenBao namespace an export that names none is written to.

preset.description: The adapters of a whole platform, one per concern: `server` (no AWS, no Kubernetes), `k8s-minimal`, `k8s-openbao`, `aws-serverless`, `aws-hybrid` (sluis on Lambda, a cluster for the workloads), `k8s-aws` (sluis as a pod on Kubernetes with AWS storage: DynamoDB, S3, KMS-wrapped signing; SSM secrets, or OpenBao with `adapters.secrets`). `aws-eks` is the deprecated name of `k8s-aws`. Absent, the preset the `platform` answers lead to; with neither, the `ports` keys decide. `adapters` and the `ports` keys override single concerns.

publicRootURL.description: The host's root, never carrying the console's mount: the bootstrap surface stays there. Unset follows `publicURL`.

publicURL.description: Where a browser reaches the console, including its mount. The admin-consent redirect URI and the values the setup steps show are built from it. Default http://localhost:8081.

recovery.description: The sign-in that needs no directory: in a cluster, a token for a ServiceAccount proven against the API server; anywhere else, a password. Unset is off for the issuer and, for the hub, on.

audience.description: The audience its token must carry.

enabled.description: Turn recovery on. Needs `inCluster`, `serviceAccount` and `audience` to be usable.

passwordSecret.description: Outside a cluster: the secret the recovery password is (`recovery/password`), read at start (the hub keeps only an Argon2id digest of it). Unset generates one and prints it, except on a function, where recovery is then off. `enabled: false` leaves it untouched and refuses the sign-in, so turning it back on needs no new password.

serviceAccount.description: The ServiceAccount whose token signs in.

release.description: The name this installation's objects carry: the Kubernetes object names (`<release>-github-orgs`, ...) and the prefix of its keys in a shared store. The chart requires it to be the release's full name.

secrets.description: How the secrets this document names are delivered (truvity/policy config.md section 5). Absent is `env`.

endpoint.description: `ssm`: overrides the SSM address, for LocalStack.

grace.description: `ssm`, layout `transition` or `v4`: how long the previous value of a rotated client secret is still accepted: the document's previous revision, while the current one is younger than this (docs/decisions/0039-the-issuer-generates-confidential-client-secrets.md, the overlap).

kmsKeyId.description: `ssm`: the id, ARN or alias of the customer-managed KMS key the parameters the service itself writes (its credentials and exports) are encrypted with. Unset, the AWS-managed `alias/aws/ssm`. The `ssm` secrets adapter's `kmsKeyId` setting; naming another there is refused.

layout.description: `ssm`: the storage layout of the installation's secrets. `v3` keeps them under `<root>/private/` and the exports controller's copies under `<root>/export/`. `transition` reads v4 first and falls back to v3, and writes every value to v4 and then to v3. `v4` keeps them under `<root>/internal/` and `<root>/external/` (docs/decisions/0041-the-secret-contract.md). Changing it is `sluis migrate secrets-layout`, never a start-time upgrade.

refresh.description: `ssm`: how old the copy may be before it is read again: a rotated secret reaches every instance within it.

region.description: `ssm`: the region. Unset follows the AWS SDK's own resolution.

root.description: `file`: the directory the secrets are mounted under. `ssm`: the installation's root, /sluis/<instance>.

source.description: `env`: the variable SLUIS_SECRET_<NAME> (the name upper-cased, every other character an underscore), for a local run. `file`: the file <root>/<name>, read on every use, so a rotated mount takes effect without a restart. `ssm`: the SecureString <root>/private/config/<name> in AWS SSM Parameter Store, every one under the prefix read at once and again after `refresh` (layout v3, root /sluis/<instance>).

secureCookies.description: Mark session cookies Secure. Unset follows the scheme the browser will use: https in the URL.

signingKey.description: The issuer's signing keys: provisioned, never minted here.

activationDelay.description: How long a newly published key waits before a replica signs with it. At least `pollInterval`.

additionalFiles.description: Every OTHER algorithm this installation signs with at once, one file per algorithm.

file.description: The primary key. Unset generates one for this process, which a local run may do and nothing else should. Exclusive with `kms`.

kms.description: Sign with AWS KMS keys instead of a file: the private key never leaves KMS. Exclusive with `file`.

additional.description: Every OTHER algorithm this installation signs with at once, each on its own rotation track, as `signingKey.additionalFiles` does for files. RS256 is the one that exists: for relying parties that need it (Kargo, EKS's OIDC provider).

keys.description: RSA_2048, RSA_3072 or RSA_4096 SIGN_VERIFY keys, oldest first, the last signing; same rotation rules as `keys`.

ECC_NIST_P384 SIGN_VERIFY keys, as ids, ARNs or aliases, oldest first. The LAST signs; the earlier ones stay published until `overlap` after the next one activates. Rotation appends a key. The role needs kms:Sign and kms:GetPublicKey on each.

region.description: The keys' region. Unset follows the AWS SDK's own resolution.

stateSecret.description: The secret (`issuer/state-secret`) holding at least 32 random bytes as base64 or hex (`openssl rand -base64 32`), the same in every replica (a replica whose secret differs refuses to start), from which the sign-in state is derived: a KMS key has no private bytes to derive from.

kmsWrapped.description: Sign with key pairs AWS KMS generates and wraps under ONE symmetric key (the `kms-wrapped` adapter): a new pair per algorithm every `rotateEvery`, published before it signs and kept after it is replaced. The private key is decrypted into process memory to sign. Exclusive with `file` and `kms`.

algorithms.description: The algorithms signed with, the first the installation default. Unset is ES384 and RS256. EdDSA is not supported yet.

keyId.description: DEPRECATED, accepted for one release with a warning: name the symmetric key as `keys.sign` instead. An alias given here is mapped onto `keys.sign`; an ARN or an id is refused.

prepublish.description: How long a new key is published before anything signs with it: longer than a verifier caches the key set (Envoy's jwt_authn: 10m). Unset is `activationDelay`.

region.description: The key's region. Unset follows the AWS SDK's own resolution.

retain.description: How long a replaced key stays published: at least `lifetimes.token` plus a skew margin. Unset is `overlap`.

rotateEvery.description: How often a new key pair is generated for each algorithm. Longer than `prepublish`, at most 168h.

stateSecret.description: The secret (`issuer/state-secret`) holding at least 32 random bytes as base64 or hex, the same in every replica, from which the sign-in state is derived: a wrapped key is replaced daily and the state must outlive it.

overlap.description: How long a rotated key stays published. Unset is `lifetimes.token` plus a margin for clock skew.

pollInterval.description: How often the files are re-read.

verifyOnly.description: PUBLIC keys published in the JWKS and never signed with, so tokens an earlier signer issued keep verifying until they expire: the overlap of a cutover from file keys to `kmsWrapped`. Each is dropped from the JWKS at its `until`. A private key stops the start.

alg.description: The key's algorithm. Unset follows the key.

file.description: A PEM public key (`PUBLIC KEY`, `RSA PUBLIC KEY`, or a certificate) or a JWK file. Never a private key.

kid.description: The `kid` the old tokens carry. Unset is the RFC 7638 thumbprint of the key, which is what a file signer derived for it.

until.description: An RFC 3339 instant after which the key is no longer published: the old tokens' last expiry, plus the verifiers' cache. Required: an overlap has an end.

store.description: Where what an operator connected is kept: `memory` keeps nothing (a restart is a fresh installation), `kubernetes` keeps it in this namespace.

valkey.description: The shared store for logins in progress and snapshots. Unset keeps both in memory, correct for one replica.

cluster.description: Speak the cluster protocol. A plain single server needs it off.

passwordSecret.description: The secret the password is (`valkey/password`). Unset connects with none.
